correctness.rationale: For the specified Paley graph over the prime field of order seventeen, exhaustive independent face reconstruction yields exactly 17 vertices, 68 edges, 68 triangles and no higher faces. The included finite certificate pairs sixteen vertices with tree edges and all other 52 edges with distinct triangles. The verifier checks all 68 disjoint pairs, all 340 Hasse cover orientations and a topological ordering; it leaves one vertex and sixteen triangles, giving the *integral* 16-sphere wedge by the discrete-Morse theorem. The affine midpoint construction is an exact equivariant bijection between edges and triangles; the signed stabilizers agree, so the oriented rational degree-one and degree-two chain representations agree. Alternating homology representations and Maschke semisimplicity identify degree-two homology as the augmentation module. The quotient statement follows from characteristic-zero transfer and exact averaging for finite actions; subgroup orders and dimension formula are checked algebraically. The 136 signed traces and midpoint equivariance were also independently enumerated. No computational experiment is extrapolated to an infinite Paley family.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant Cioabă–Mim paper studies clique H1 and conference graphs, but its conference-family vanishing theorem is for graphs with at least 256 vertices and does not imply the Paley-17 integral homotopy type or its affine H2 character. The nearest same-graph published result describes its Lovász neighborhood complex, a different simplicial construction. Paley-17 is self-complementary, so independence-complex synonyms were queried. MathWorld provides known graph structure, clique number and symmetry facts, not this topological theorem. Search results yielded no equivalent or stronger Paley-17 clique/independence homotopy-and-affine quotient result; completeness of all publications is not asserted.

value.rationale: The 17-vertex Paley graph is the canonical extremal Ramsey graph without a four-clique or four-independent-set and a small conference graph of exceptional interest in the recent Cioabă–Mim homological investigation. The result supplies a complete integral homotopy decomposition, not merely the known clique face vector or Euler characteristic. The affine midpoint construction reveals a full rational representation on a natural group of 136 symmetries, and the subgroup formula determines all geometric affine-quotient rational Betti numbers. This is a motivated exact classification for a canonical finite object; it requires a genuine acyclic matching certificate and a nontrivial equivariant chain-module comparison. No invented broader consequence, all-parameter theorem or significance beyond the specified graph is invoked.
